content_md: There was a time when half the readers I met would say something like “I’ve read everything you’ve written” which is a lot. I used to call it the “ribbonfarm absurdity marathon” because it’s something I’d never do.  But the blogosphere had that culture and rewarded such personality. You  discovered what felt like a great secret subworld and it felt like a portal to a mini alt-reality. But that culture broke around 2016 with the culture war. Hidden treasure vibes gave way to conspiratorial den vibes. Sensible people sensibly retreated. The subterranean caves got colonized by paranoiac cults. Substack offered a bougie mall experience but this did not reward the same nerdy obsessive personality. Even long-term readers I’d say read less than half my stuff. I now assume that if someone says they read me, it’s a shallower basic awareness. Perhaps the glance at 3/10 emails and read 1 in 10. Partly of course my writing has changed a lot but I think the media environment has changed more.
